description:
## Goal

Make `RuntimeDemand(E)` an ordinary change-driven fact formula and delete the whole-cone product calculation. A newly discovered callable edge becomes one exact dependency and contribution; it never causes standing values to reset and replay from bottom.

This is the main proven cold-compilation hotspot and the central spreadsheet-model repair after product state survives across requests.

## Boundary with InputDemand

`RuntimeDemand(E)` is executable materialization demand. `InputDemand(F)` is source-function activation-key precision and is converted separately by `fz-kdt.213`. They remain distinct fact keys, values, producers, and readers. They may reuse generic World fact/contribution plumbing, but they do not share a cone, SCC solver, dirty index, bridge, or compatibility path. `fz-kdt.165` extends InputDemand; it does not add a RuntimeDemand dimension.

## Recorded signal

On `00420_enum_take_drop_split`, one cold debug-interp request produced eight demand-cone settlements: two one-member cones, four 198-member cones, and two 204-member cones. The large cones each climbed 17 rounds and ran 1,028 or 1,068 member derivations; `external_members` was zero throughout. A debug sampling profile placed roughly one quarter of captured main-thread stacks within runtime-demand production.

`produce_runtime_demand_product` collects a transitive cone, settles every member from bottom, discovers actual callable-flow edges from the result, and may discard and repeat the calculation. One product key therefore hides a program-scale unit of work.

## Correct model

- `RuntimeDemand(E)` has one FactKey, one authoritative World slot, and one producer formula.
- A formula reads settled executable facts, its Current exact input-contribution cell, Current direct-target demand cells, and Current root-and-function-keyed callable-input projections. Recorded absence is bottom; no formula waits for a peer demand to become settled. A retained root explicitly owns the executable-need seed for its exact entry and retracts that seed with its lifecycle; there is no formula-local Whole fallback when the last caller disappears.
- `RuntimeDemandCallableInputs(R, F)` contains only correlated activation-input and input-demand rows for one typed root/function pair. Each executable owns/replaces one row under its root and function; executable identity remains contribution provenance, never inventory in the semantic payload. Roots cannot contribute to or wake another root’s projection.
- A formula with no live owner and bottom demand publishes no callable-input row or outbound target contribution; exact replacement retracts its former frontier.
- Before every direct peer cell exists, an owned formula publishes its provisional `RuntimeDemand(E)`, any nonempty callable-input row, and the exact direct return contributions derived solely from caller-local use. It waits only for missing Current peer presence before publishing peer-dependent capture/input and first-class target contributions. A formula with no owner publishes no outbound contribution. This seeds acyclic callees without a bottom-only round and bootstraps self and mutual cycles without a settled-peer dependency or a Whole fallback.
- Each caller owns replaceable contributions to exact target cells. Retraction removes only that caller contribution.
- Cyclic convergence comes from ordinary content-changing wakes and transitive settledness.
- Artifact and transport consumers wait on settled demand facts.
- A dormant persistent root session receives resulting fact movements through exact subscriptions.

Preserve `ExecutableRuntimeDemand` as one semantic projection unless causal evidence proves independently moving fields cause false wakes. Do not split cells speculatively.

## TDD and telemetry acceptance

1. Acyclic, self-recursive, and mutual-recursive formulas converge with exact contributions, provisional bottom publication, and no settled-peer waits.
2. Callable-edge addition, replacement, and retraction preserve unaffected values and evaluate only exact readers. Cross-root callable projections remain disjoint, and a formerly reached executable returns to bottom after its last owner retracts.
3. Same persistent root and unreachable redefinition evaluate zero demand formulas; a reached edit evaluates only the transitive reader closure.
4. Every non-initial evaluation names moved content. Readiness-only movement causes zero demand calculation. Equal conclusions do not revise facts or wake readers.
5. Several scheduler orders produce identical semantic facts, causal work multiset, backend program, and three-door output.
6. No cone, round, SCC, root, or executable-inventory scan occurs; acceptance uses deterministic work, never a wall-clock threshold.

Before deleting cone telemetry, census `external_members` across the full matrix. Any observed external/displacement path becomes a focused retraction/finality test; if none is observed, delete the path with its owner.

## Required deletion

- `collect_demand_cone`, `settle_demand_cone`, `DemandConeRetryGuard`, `DemandGraph`, `SettledDemandCone`, and `actual_flow_edges`;
- demand-specific dirty sets and reverse indexes;
- PullSession return/input contribution, contributor, joined-demand, callee-inventory, and bespoke invalidation maps;
- whole-cone publication/replay telemetry and atomic-product documentation;
- temporary shadow facts, compatibility bridges, and comparison harnesses.

Run focused fact/scheduler/product tests, full library, serial fixture matrix, both large target fixtures on all doors, cross-process determinism, formatting, check, strict clippy, and docs. Rewrite fact-engine, pipeline, semantic-fixpoint, performance instrumentation, and `northstar.html` around the ordinary reactive formula and record every removed authority.

## Retained-root return boundary

The RuntimeDemand cutover and the retained-root return boundary are one atomic step: base reactive facts already invalidate and re-drive exact product readers correctly, while RuntimeDemandInput and DeriveRuntimeDemand exist only after this ticket. Add a focused retained-session RED that holds a cached root, moves an exact leaf RuntimeDemand input from Ignore to Whole, and proves the resulting DeriveRuntimeDemand wake is drained before return. The returned artifact must retain the exact current settled demand and corresponding Whole-dependent layout; affected product generations must reproject, equal reproduction must do no demand/product work, and no ready work capable of changing the requested root may remain. Use existing exact queues and dependencies—no global quiescence scan, blanket rerun, or second queue.

## Callable target identity boundary

`CallableConstructionTarget(owner ExecutableKey, local ValueId, grounded CallableSurface)` is one exact demand-driven World fact whose value is the canonical target ExecutableKey. Its sole producer reads settled current ExecutableFacts(owner), resolves that local construction’s function and complete capture-type vector, waits on the callee function’s Recursive and InputDemand facts, and only then mints and publishes the exact canonical target. Owner redefinition replaces or retracts the fact; equal reproduction preserves its revision and wakes nobody.

DeriveRuntimeDemand reads Current only for the exact grounded construction-target keys its semantic derivation demands. While a target is absent, it publishes provisional RuntimeDemand and its callable-input row, withholds only the affected outbound contribution, and waits for that exact fact. It never mints a type, structural address, or activation key and never scans callable publishers, activations, executable inventories, or speculative surfaces. Direct call edges continue to use their settled CallableTarget evidence. No executable identity enters the root-and-function callable-input semantic payload.

The immutable Ty-to-RuntimeDemandTypeProjection memo is World-owned and shared by ExecutableFacts construction and RuntimeDemand reads. RuntimeDemand evaluation is lookup-only; it cannot mint identities.

Focused construction-target acceptance covers static escaped bootstrap, an arbitrary late grounded surface, self and mutual bootstrap, independent surfaces, exact missing-prerequisite waits, owner replacement and retraction, equal reproduction without revision or wake, unchanged RuntimeDemand formula identity inventory, and absence of contributor scans or speculative target minting.


## Exact capture-row correlation

Capture-row correlation uses exact target provenance. Direct callable demands select a root-and-function row by their typed CallableTarget surface and activation frame. First-class demands name exact CallableConstructionTarget keys; present target facts and loaded callable-input rows can reveal further live local callable functions or surfaces. The same formula follows only those newly named keys in a finite local dependency-discovery loop until its typed read set stops growing, then selects each correlated row through the exact owner/value/surface-to-target mapping. The standalone-addressed raw capture prefix is not an authority: a precise capture Ty can legitimately key to an erased activation-frame Ty. No raw capture-prefix fallback remains.

## Exact delivered-lane consequence

Removing the cone anchor also removes its unrelated `ExecutableNeed::Value -> Whole` return widening. A directly selected clause may therefore project only the fields its caller consumes: for `Enum.count`, the statically known `:ok` tag is `Ignore`, the integer payload is `Whole`, and backend/native transport carries exactly one `RawInt` lane. Tests prove the complete demand-to-layout-to-adapter chain instead of pinning an incidental aggregate lane count. Boxed first-class owners still contribute their exact executable-need return demand independently.
title: Replace RuntimeDemand cone replay with reactive per-executable facts
